Danielle

messages.subject_clean: object of type 'closure' is not subsettable data
messages.body_plain:
If data1 is a reactive expression, then the way to read it is data1(), not data1. e.g. instead of data1[!is.na <http://is.na>(data1$consent),] it'd be data1()[!is.na <http://is.na>(data1()$consent),]

messages.subject: Some way to reset (or forget) an input value: Or how to reuse an input widget
messages.subject_clean: Some way to reset (or forget) an input value: Or how to reuse an input widget
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

my problem comes from a specific situation. I want to create a shiny app for a kind of survey.
For many reasons, I've discarded the option to present the different questions at the same time,
and I'm trying to do it sequentially (one at a time), which seems more rational and even aesthetically better.

Essentially, I show the question and the choices with radioButtons, and another widgets allow the
user to move back and forward in the questions list. Every time the user moves, I update the radioButtons
to adapt it to current choices and previous answer if done.

I keep the answers for every question in an array, inside an observeEvent for the radioButtons id.

My problem is that sometimes the observer does not react. Specifically, when the user repeats the
answer. Imagine this as follows: user answers "Yes" in question 1 and "Yes" again in question 2. But the
observer does not take any action the second time because there is no change in the input, although
the list of choices at update had nothing selected (using selected=character(0)) with the second question.

The trivial solution would be to erase the input but, as you know perfectly, this is not possible.

Do you know any trick to solve this issue?

Can you give me any clue about a completely new approach for this situation? Right now, I have
the least idea how to see out of the problem.

Thanks in advance

José Antonio

messages.subject_clean: Some way to reset (or forget) an input value: Or how to reuse an input widget
messages.body_plain:
Hi José,

Would you be able to provide a minimal reproducible example of this problem? From what I could infer, the problem is that the observer is listening to the radioButtons input value, so it will not be triggered if the user selects the same option consecutively.

As a workaround, you could reset the radioButtons input each time the user navigates to a new question using the shinyjs package, i.e. observeEvent(input$question, shinyjs::reset('radio_id')). Would this work for you?

Alternatively, you could create a radioButtons group for each question and attach an observer to each of those groups.

Best regards,

Monica

messages.subject_clean: Some way to reset (or forget) an input value: Or how to reuse an input widget
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

pity, this reset function seemed promising, but it does not work in my case because the initial value is "nothing" (I don't want any default),
that is why I chose character(0) for the selected parameter.

A solution may be to take: (o) no answer   ( ) Yes    ( ) No,       but it's ugly and it's the last in my list of solutions.

I've found an example, and I've reduced it as much as possible. If someone is able to make it run suitably, I'd appreciate it much.

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    useShinyjs(),
    div(
      id = "form",
      radioButtons("gender", "Gender", c("Male", "Female"), selected=character(0))
    ),
    actionButton("resetGender", "Reset Gender")
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {

    observeEvent(input$resetGender, {
      reset("gender")
    })

  }
)
You can see that after any option ('female') is chosen, the option does not disappear when you click on reset.

An alternative that I envisage is something like that: many different widgets, each one with its id, Z1, Z2, ...
When I move forward to the next question, I have to remove the Z1 widget and put the Z2 widget; the observer
would be just one, as I know which is the active question (something like observeEvent(eval(parse(text=paste0("input$Z",aux))), { ... )

However, I don't know how to deactivate and activate the widget, since it's a different operation than updateRadioButtons.

Looking forward to hear your ideas.

JA

messages.body_plain:
Yea, sorry, the documentation says that using character(0) is discouraged as you can't return to that state. So updateRadioButtons(session, 'gender', selected = character(0)) doesn't work either.

If each question has the same set of choices, then could you rerender the radio buttons each time the user navigates to a new question? You could keep track of the active question and store its response using an observer. E.g.

library(shiny)
library(shinyjs)

qs = 1:3

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    useShinyjs(),

    selectInput('question', 'Choose question', qs),

    div(
      id = "form",

      uiOutput('radioUI')

    )
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {

    rv = reactiveValues(responses = character(length(qs)), current = NULL)

    output$radioUI <- renderUI({

      input$question

      radioButtons("options", "Gender", c("Male", "Female"), selected = character(0))

    })

    observeEvent(input$question, {
      rv$current = as.numeric(input$question)
    })

    observeEvent(input$options, {
      rv$responses[rv$current] <- input$options
    })

    observe(print(rv$responses))
  }
)

Alternatively, if each question has a different set of choices, then you could create a unique widget for each question and an accompanying observer to record the user's response to that question:

library(shiny)
library(shinyjs)

qs = 1:3

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    useShinyjs(),

    selectInput('question', 'Choose question', qs),

    div(
      id = "form",

      lapply(
        X = qs,
        FUN = function(x) {

          conditionalPanel(
            condition = paste('input.question == ', x),
            uiOutput(paste0('radioUI', x))
            )

        })

    )
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {

    rv = reactiveValues(responses = character(length(qs)))

    lapply(qs, function(x) {

      id = paste0("options", x)

      output[[paste0('radioUI', x)]] <- renderUI({
        radioButtons(paste0("options", x), "Gender", c("Male", "Female"), selected = character(0))
      })

      observeEvent(input[[id]], {
        rv$responses[[x]] <- input[[id]]
      })

    })

    observe(print(rv$responses))
  }
)

messages.body_plain:
No worries! I've never used reactives in a conditionalPanel condition so I'm not entirely sure how that would work, but using outputOptions(output, 'foo', suspendWhenHidden = F) seems to do something similar to what you're after: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38895710/passing-reactive-values-to-conditionalpanel-condition
https://shinydata.wordpress.com/2015/02/02/a-few-things-i-learned-about-shiny-and-reactive-programming/#conditional-panel
Or you could use setInputValue(): https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/communicating-with-js.html

Also, my apologies but I seemed to have posted an earlier version of the first solution in my post. The updated one is below, it uses updateRadioButtons to update the radio buttons each time it is rerendered (i.e. whenever the user changes questions):

library(shiny)
library(shinyjs)

qs = 1:3

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    useShinyjs(),
    selectInput('question', 'Choose question', qs),
    div(
      id = "form",
      uiOutput('radioUI')
    )
  ),

  server = function(input, output, session) {

    rv = reactiveValues(responses = character(length(qs)), current = NULL)

    output$radioUI <- renderUI({

      input$question

      radioButtons("options", "Gender", c("Male", "Female"), selected = character(0))

    })

    observeEvent(input$question, {
      rv$current = as.numeric(input$question)

      if(!is.null(rv$responses[rv$current])) updateRadioButtons(session, 'options', selected = rv$responses[rv$current])

    })

    observeEvent(input$options, {
      rv$responses[rv$current] <- input$options
    })

    observe(print(rv$responses))
  }
)
